item.title: Why we pay taxes
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description:
Photo by Mikhail Nilov, Pexels

I’ve been genuinely curious about attitudes towards taxation. Decades ago, I got a stern look from a Swiss colleague. I’d just found out about their keenness for having a referendum and wanted to know why they didn’t have one to abolish tax. He just looked at me in a very disappointed way and just said it would be highly irresponsible. Now, no-one likes paying tax. But I think we all know why we pay tax. However, I’ve been thinking that it’s not a simple transaction. It’s not just that I need medical support now and again, or quite like having a few roads around the place. What I’ve never been able to articulate is that taxation is so much more than a club membership. And certainly, as some would have it, it is most definitely not a confiscation of private wealth, instead, it the price of having a functioning currency, a working legal system, and a stable economy in which private wealth can exist at all.
